trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Disney World, Orlando, Florida
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando Boutique Stay
hotel.location: Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista, Orlando

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 13:00. Take the Magical Express or a budget rideshare (Lyft/Uber) to your boutique stay near Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with your resort map and park schedule. Pick up a Disney park app and plan your week using the free Disney World app to identify low-wait times and free entertainment.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely stroll to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket needed). Browse the shops, enjoy the waterfront atmosphere, and catch free live music performances at the West Side or Marketplace stages. This is a great low-cost way to soak in the Disney magic on arrival night.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or a fast-casual spot near your hotel upon arrival — try Subway or McDonald's near Hotel Plaza Blvd for budget-friendly options under $10.
meals.dinner: Head to Disney Springs and dine at The Polite Pig — a budget-friendly BBQ spot with plates starting around $14–$18. Alternatively, grab a quick-service meal at Chicken Guy! for around $10–$13.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your multi-day park tickets in advance online for the best savings. Consider a 5-day Magic Kingdom base ticket. Download the My Disney Experience app before arrival to book Lightning Lane selections and check wait times. Pick up a refillable resort mug if your hotel offers one for savings on drinks throughout the week.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Magic Kingdom early (park opening, typically 9:00 AM — check the app). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and then Fantasyland for Seven Dwarfs Mine Train using the virtual queue or Lightning Lane. Use the free Genie planning tool in the app to minimize wait times. Explore Cinderella Castle and catch the opening welcome show.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy classic rides like Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Grab a mid-afternoon snack and take a break during the hottest part of the day (typically 1–3 PM). Watch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (check schedule on app) which is included with park admission.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the TRON Lightcycle Run (if available) and end the night with the spectacular Happily Ever After fireworks show over Cinderella Castle — one of the best free-with-admission experiences at Disney. This is a must-see on your first full park day.

meals.breakfast: Eat a filling breakfast at your hotel before heading to the park to save money. Grab a banana or granola bar from a grocery store snack stash.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — a budget-friendly quick-service spot. Try the Lighthouse Sandwich or Fried Fish Basket for around $12–$15. Great air-conditioned seating too.
meals.dinner: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn and Cafe in Frontierland — hearty Tex-Mex quick-service meals for $12–$16. Load up at the free toppings bar to stretch your meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and bring a refillable water bottle — water is available free of charge at any quick-service counter inside the park. Apply sunscreen regularly as June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 88–95°F). Arrive 30 minutes before park opening for the best ride access.

day_by_day.morning: Head to EPCOT for rope drop (park opening). Start in World Discovery with Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (join the virtual queue at exactly park open time via the app — it's free). Then ride Test Track and Mission: SPACE for a space-themed adventure morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the World Showcase, which opens at 11:00 AM. Walk the 1.2-mile promenade around World Showcase Lagoon visiting international pavilions. Sample affordable snacks from different countries — a great budget way to 'eat around the world.' Try a crepe in France (~$6), a pretzel in Germany (~$5), or spring rolls in China (~$6). Watch the free cultural performances in each pavilion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's Luminous The Global Celebration nighttime spectacular over the lagoon — included with park admission and absolutely stunning. Grab a final snack from the Canada or UK pavilion before heading back to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack your own snacks and a piece of fruit to eat before entering the park.
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land Pavilion — one of EPCOT's best-value quick-service restaurants. Meals range from $11–$16 with rotating seasonal options including sandwiches, Asian noodle bowls, and rotisserie chicken.
meals.dinner: Snack your way around World Showcase for a fun and budget-friendly dinner — budget $20–$25 total for a variety of international bites from 3–4 pavilions instead of a sit-down restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is a walking-heavy park — comfortable footwear is essential. The World Showcase is perfect for families as kids enjoy the interactive 'Agent P's World Showcase Adventure' scavenger hunt (free with admission). Check the EPCOT app page for live entertainment schedules throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hollywood Studios at rope drop. Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (walk-on or short wait at opening). Then join the boarding group queue for Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance, one of the most immersive theme park experiences ever created. Explore Batuu and enjoy the Star Wars atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Alien Swirling Saucers. Then catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times — it's free with admission and very entertaining for all ages). Walk through the Hollywood Boulevard area and catch the Citizens of Hollywood street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the Fantasmic! nighttime show (check schedule — typically two showings on busy summer nights). This is a spectacular water, fire, and projection show featuring classic Disney villains and heroes — completely included with park admission. A perfect Hollywood Studios finale.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the hotel or bring snacks. Alternatively, grab a Ronto Wrap from Ronto Roasters in Galaxy's Edge for a fun Star Wars-themed breakfast option (~$13–$15).
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — a fan-favorite quick-service spot with affordable and creative menu items like the Totchos (tater tot nachos) and BBQ Brisket Melt for $11–$14.
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary near Hollywood Boulevard — one of the most budget-friendly table-service alternatives with quick-service options like burgers, wraps, and international plates for $12–$16.

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is one of Disney's most popular parks in summer — arrive at least 20 minutes before opening. Use the Lightning Lane Multi Pass for Slinky Dog Dash if the wait exceeds 60 minutes. The Fantasmic! Dining Package exists but is not necessary on a budget — arrive 45–60 minutes early for a good seat in the free standby section.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at Animal Kingdom — arrive at rope drop. Head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the most popular ride at Animal Kingdom — join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane early). Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a beautiful, immersive experience through bioluminescent rainforest scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa and ride Kilimanjaro Safaris — a free-roaming safari through 110 acres with real African animals including giraffes, elephants, lions, and rhinos. Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for a free walking experience with gorillas and exotic birds. Catch a performance of Festival of the Lion King — a Broadway-caliber show included with park admission.
day_by_day.evening: End the day at Discovery Island and watch the Tree of Life Awakenings — a projection show on the iconic 145-foot Tree of Life that runs every 10–15 minutes after dark, completely free with admission. Head back to the hotel for a restful evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or pack snacks. Grab a Pongu Pongu Lumpia (pineapple cream cheese spring roll) in Pandora as a fun morning treat (~$5).
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney World's best quick-service restaurants with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken for $14–$18. Beautiful outdoor seating with views of the waterways.
meals.dinner: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — a fan-favorite with customizable grain bowls and protein options for $14–$17. Healthy, filling, and great value. Try the Blueberry Cream Cheese Mousse for dessert (~$5).

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (typically 8–9 PM in summer). Plan your day accordingly. June heat is intense at Animal Kingdom — the park has less shade than others, so bring a hat, sunscreen, and a cooling towel. The Kilimanjaro Safari is best in the morning when animals are most active.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget-friendly break from the parks and visit Disney's BoardWalk (free admission — no park ticket needed). Walk the lakeside promenade, watch street performers, rent a surrey bike (~$25/30 min for a family bike), and enjoy the early morning atmosphere before the crowds arrive. This is a great low-cost Disney experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your favorite park for a half-day visit or revisit Magic Kingdom to catch any rides or shows you missed on Day 2. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the hotel pool (free) to relax and recharge. If you have energy, revisit EPCOT's World Showcase for more snacking and exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Disney Springs again for the evening — catch a free concert at the Marketplace Stage or West Side, browse the World of Disney store (the largest Disney merchandise store in the world), and enjoy the festive atmosphere. This is a perfect low-cost evening activity.

meals.breakfast: Cook a simple breakfast in your hotel room if you have kitchen access, or grab pastries and coffee from a nearby grocery store or gas station to save money.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a grocery store (Publix on S. Apopka Vineland Rd is nearby) — sandwiches, fruit, chips, and drinks for a family of 4 can cost under $20 total, a huge budget win.
meals.dinner: Disney Springs dining: Try The Daily Poutine for affordable loaded fries (~$8–$12) or grab a pizza slice from Pizza Ponte (~$6–$8 per slice). Both are casual, delicious, and budget-friendly options.

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally lighter to prevent park fatigue — a common issue on multi-day Disney trips, especially with children. Use this day to do laundry, repack, charge devices, and review your final day plans. Visit a nearby Publix or Walmart to stock up on snacks, water, and sunscreen to save money for the final park day.

day_by_day.morning: Return to your favorite park one last time — Magic Kingdom is recommended for a memorable final Disney morning. Ride any must-do attractions you haven't experienced yet. Take time to soak in the atmosphere, snap photos in front of Cinderella Castle, and enjoy the magic before your trip ends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your last afternoon doing any final shopping for souvenirs. Pro budget tip: Buy souvenirs at Disney Springs rather than inside the parks (same merchandise, easier browsing, no park ticket needed). The World of Disney store has the widest selection. Alternatively, pick up Disney-themed items at a nearby Target or Walmart for significantly lower prices.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel, pack your bags, and prepare for departure. Enjoy a relaxed final dinner near the hotel. Reflect on an incredible week at Walt Disney World. If your flight is the next morning, get to bed early for a fresh start.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick and hearty breakfast at your hotel or a nearby IHOP or Denny's on Hotel Plaza Blvd — budget around $8–$12 per person for a filling start to your last full day.
meals.lunch: Casey's Corner on Main Street USA in Magic Kingdom — an iconic Disney hot dog and corn dog nugget spot. Meals run $10–$14 and the location on Main Street USA makes for a classic Disney dining memory.
meals.dinner: Celebrate your final night with a slightly more indulgent (but still budget-conscious) meal at Raglan Road Irish Pub at Disney Springs — live Irish music, great atmosphere, and shareable plates for $15–$22 per person. Happy hour specials available on drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with your boutique hotel. Most hotels allow you to store luggage at the front desk so you can continue enjoying the parks after checkout. Keep all park tickets, MagicBands, and receipts organized. Total estimated park budget for the week (excluding tickets): approximately $40–$60/day on food and extras per person if you follow quick-service and snack strategies. Multi-day tickets purchased in advance can save 20–30% versus single-day pricing.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Orlando International Airport to Magic Kingdom area hotel via Disney's Magical Express or rideshare (~45–60 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket needed) for a relaxed first afternoon. Explore the shops, browse World of Disney, and soak in the Disney atmosphere without the pressure of a full park day.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening — enjoy live music at the House of Blues or Raglan Road Irish Pub, catch a street performer, and browse the entertainment district. Great low-key introduction to the Disney experience.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport before or during your flight.
meals.lunch: Grab a casual meal at Disney Springs — try D-Luxe Burger or Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza for a quick, affordable option (~$12–18 per person).
meals.dinner: Raglan Road Irish Pub & Restaurant at Disney Springs — lively atmosphere, live Irish music, and hearty pub fare. Expect ~$20–35 per person. Make a reservation in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pick up your park tickets or MagicBands at the hotel if pre-ordered. Download the My Disney Experience app and link your reservations. Purchase a refillable resort mug if staying on-site. Rest early — big park days start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day — Arrive at rope drop (park opens ~9:00 AM, arrive by 8:30 AM). Hit the most popular rides first: Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Use Lightning Lane passes strategically for headliner attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom — ride Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and It's a Small World. Catch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically around 3:00 PM). Take a midday break at the hotel if needed to avoid peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Magic Kingdom Fireworks Spectacular (Happily Ever After, typically at 9:00 PM). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. about 45 minutes early. Ride a few lower-wait attractions during the fireworks when crowds thin.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick pastry and coffee at Main Street Bakery inside Magic Kingdom.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — counter-service seafood and sandwiches, quiet seating upstairs, ~$14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland (table service) — French-inspired cuisine in the Beast's enchanted castle. Book well in advance. ~$25–40 per person. Alternatively, Skipper Canteen for a fun themed experience.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes and bring sunscreen, hats, and a poncho (Florida afternoon storms are common in June). June is peak season — Lightning Lane Multi Pass is strongly recommended. Park hours may extend to 11:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Arrive at EPCOT for rope drop (~9:00 AM). Start in Future World / World Discovery: ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (book Individual Lightning Lane early), Test Track, and Spaceship Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the World Showcase beginning at 11:00 AM when it opens. Sample authentic foods from countries including Japan (sushi, mochi), Morocco (shawarma), France (crêpes), and Mexico (tacos). Browse artisan shops and cultural exhibits in each pavilion.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's HARMONIOUS nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (one of the largest fireworks shows Disney has ever created). Find a spot near the America pavilion for a great view. Explore illuminated pavilions post-show.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel before heading out.
meals.lunch: World Showcase grazing — budget ~$30–40 per person sampling 4–5 countries. Try a school bread from Norway, tacos from Mexico, and a crepe from France.
meals.dinner: Via Napoli Ristorante e Pizzeria in the Italy pavilion — authentic Neapolitan pizza in a beautiful setting. ~$20–35 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is one of the largest Disney parks — wear comfortable walking shoes. The World Showcase is ideal for adults and older kids; younger children may prefer Future World attractions. Check for any EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival events running in June.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure. Arrive at rope drop to secure a boarding group or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance (the most in-demand ride at Walt Disney World). Head straight to Galaxy's Edge and explore Black Spire Outpost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Build your own lightsaber at Savi's Workshop (book in advance, ~$250 per lightsaber — optional splurge) or build a droid at Droid Depot (~$120). Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Then explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: Toy Story Land (Slinky Dog Dash), Rock 'n' Roller Coaster, and Tower of Terror.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the Fantasmic! nighttime show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (typically 8:00 or 9:00 PM). Arrive 30–45 minutes early for good seats. This classic Disney show features Mickey Mouse, water screens, and fireworks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel before heading to the park.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo in Galaxy's Edge — Star Wars-themed counter service with creative dishes like Fried Endorian Tip-Yip (chicken). ~$15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — eat in vintage cars under a starlit sky watching classic sci-fi movie clips. Fun, unique atmosphere. ~$20–35 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop and Droid Depot require advance reservations and are premium experiences — plan and budget accordingly. Hollywood Studios is the most 'teen and adult' friendly park. June heat peaks in the afternoon; use indoor attractions as a break.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom — Kilimanjaro Safaris. Arrive at rope drop for the best wildlife sightings when animals are most active in the cooler morning hours. See lions, elephants, giraffes, hippos, and more on this 18-minute open-air safari.
day_by_day.afternoon: Avatar: Flight of Passage in Pandora – The World of Avatar (use Lightning Lane — this is the park's most popular ride). Explore the bioluminescent world of Pandora, ride Na'vi River Journey, and walk the Valley of Mo'ara. Also visit Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (you will get wet!).
day_by_day.evening: Rivers of Light nighttime spectacular at Animal Kingdom (check schedule — show times vary). Afterward, head back to the hotel for a relaxed evening or visit Disney Springs for dessert and shopping.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel — fuel up before the safari.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — healthy, flavorful bowls with rice, grains, and proteins. One of the best counter-service options at Disney. ~$14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia — Asian-inspired cuisine in a beautiful lodge-style setting. ~$20–35 per person. Reserve in advance. Alternatively, head to Disney Springs for a wider dining selection.

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks (~8:00–9:00 PM). Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. The park is heavily shaded compared to others, making it slightly more comfortable in June heat. Early morning is best for safari and Avatar.

day_by_day.morning: Flex / Revisit Day — Return to your favorite park for any missed attractions or re-rides. Alternatively, spend the morning at the hotel pool, which is a great way to relax and let kids enjoy the resort amenities. Many Disney resort pools have waterslides and themed features.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Afternoon — Browse unique shops like Marketplace Co-Op, The LEGO Store, and Basin. Visit the NBA Experience or Splitsville Luxury Lanes (bowling + dining) for family fun. Great for souvenir shopping on a mid-range budget.
day_by_day.evening: Special Farewell Dinner at Disney Springs — celebrate the trip with a sit-down dinner at a standout restaurant. Great options include The BOATHOUSE (waterfront dining with fresh seafood) or STK Orlando (upscale steakhouse). Enjoy live entertainment in the area afterward.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed hotel breakfast — enjoy the resort dining room or grab pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: Earl of Sandwich at Disney Springs — fresh, affordable sandwiches. ~$10–14 per person. A Disney Springs fan favorite.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — fresh seafood, steaks, and pasta with a beautiful waterfront view. ~$35–55 per person. Reserve in advance for this popular spot.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is typically the busiest park day of the week — a resort pool or Disney Springs day is a smart, crowd-avoiding choice. Use this day for souvenir shopping and to recharge. Check if your hotel has any special evening events or character meet-and-greets.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning — Depending on your departure time, enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Pack and check out (most hotels offer luggage storage so you can enjoy the resort until your flight). Take a final stroll around the hotel grounds and take photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before departure, visit Disney Springs one last time for any last-minute souvenirs or a quick treat — try a Dole Whip, Mickey-shaped pretzel, or LeFou's Brew for a sweet send-off. Alternatively, spend final hours at the hotel pool.
day_by_day.evening: Depart for Orlando International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for travel time and security. Disney's Magical Express or a rideshare will take approximately 45–60 minutes to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Resort hotel breakfast — enjoy a full sit-down or buffet meal as a relaxed final morning treat. ~$15–25 per person.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Disney Springs or hotel quick service before heading to the airport.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Check out is typically 11:00 AM — ask the front desk about late checkout or luggage storage. Confirm your return flight details and arrange airport transportation the night before. Don't forget to check all hotel rooms for left-behind items. Consider mailing heavier souvenirs home to avoid baggage fees.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from Orlando International Airport to your boutique stay at Magic Kingdom, Lake Buena Vista. Settle into your premium accommodations and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort Orientation & Disney Springs Exploration — Head to Disney Springs for a leisurely afternoon stroll. Browse world-class boutiques, visit the LEGO Store, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. No park ticket required, making it a perfect low-key arrival afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening — Enjoy live entertainment at the Marketplace and Pleasure Island districts. Take in a performance or two from local artists performing throughout the Springs.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or grab a light snack upon landing at the airport lounge.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Morimoto Asia at Disney Springs — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship restaurant offering Pan-Asian cuisine including sushi, dim sum, and signature wagyu dishes in an upscale setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at STK Orlando at Disney Springs — A modern American steakhouse offering premium USDA dry-aged steaks, fresh seafood, and craft cocktails with a lively upscale ambiance. Reserve the chef's tasting menu for a true luxury experience.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in through your concierge in advance to ensure your room is ready upon arrival. Consider purchasing Disney MagicBand+ for seamless park access throughout the trip. Confirm all dining reservations made via Disney's advance dining reservation system (up to 60 days ahead).

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park — Arrive at rope drop (park opening, typically 9:00 AM) using your resort's complimentary Early Theme Park Entry benefit (30 minutes before official opening). Prioritize Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, Tron Lightcycle / Run, and Space Mountain using Lightning Lane Premier Pass for zero wait times. Explore Fantasyland and Tomorrowland in the cool morning hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Magic Kingdom Continued — After lunch, explore Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean and Jungle Cruise. Visit Liberty Square for the Haunted Mansion. Use Lightning Lane selections strategically for any remaining top-tier attractions. Catch the afternoon parade along Main Street U.S.A. for a quintessential Disney moment.
day_by_day.evening: Happily Ever After Fireworks Spectacular — Position yourselves on Main Street U.S.A. or reserve a premium fireworks dessert party at Tomorrowland Terrace for reserved viewing with exclusive desserts, beverages, and an unobstructed sightline of Cinderella Castle illuminated in stunning projection mapping.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Be Our Guest Restaurant inside Magic Kingdom — Dine in the enchanted Beast's Castle with a prix-fixe breakfast menu. Reserve well in advance as this is one of the most sought-after Disney dining experiences.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skipper Canteen inside Magic Kingdom — A hidden gem offering globally inspired cuisine in a quirky, adventurer-themed setting. Try the Jungle Juice and signature Sustainable Fish of the Day.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cinderella's Royal Table inside Cinderella Castle — A once-in-a-lifetime fine dining experience inside the iconic castle with princess character meet-and-greets, prix-fixe menu featuring premium beef tenderloin and Maine lobster bisque.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Lightning Lane Premier Pass (formerly Genie+) for Magic Kingdom to skip queues on all major attractions. Wear comfortable premium footwear — expect 8–12 miles of walking. Stay hydrated as June temperatures in Orlando regularly exceed 90°F (32°C) with high humidity. Apply sunscreen liberally throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour — Arrive at EPCOT using Early Entry benefit. Begin with Future World (now Epcot's World Discovery and World Nature areas) — experience Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (Lightning Lane a must), Test Track, and Soarin' Around the World. Then transition to the World Showcase as pavilions open around 11:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: EPCOT World Showcase Deep Dive — Spend the afternoon touring pavilions from Japan, France, Morocco, Italy, and Canada. Sample authentic cuisines and artisan beverages at each stop. Visit the France pavilion for Remy's Ratatouille Adventure and enjoy a crêpe from the outdoor kiosk. Browse unique international artisan goods and cultural exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: EPCOT Harmonious Nighttime Spectacular — One of the largest nighttime shows ever created for a Disney park. Secure a premium lakeside spot around World Showcase Lagoon or book the EPCOT Forever Fireworks Dessert Party for VIP reserved waterfront seating with unlimited premium desserts and specialty drinks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Sunshine Seasons inside The Land Pavilion at EPCOT — Fresh, farm-to-table options including house-made granola, artisan pastries, and egg dishes made with produce grown in EPCOT's very own greenhouses.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion — Authentic Japanese teppanyaki dining experience with skilled chefs preparing wagyu beef, seafood, and seasonal vegetables tableside in an elegant setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Monsieur Paul in the France Pavilion — EPCOT's most refined dining experience. A French haute cuisine restaurant inspired by legendary chef Paul Bocuse, offering a prix-fixe menu with dishes like foie gras, duck confit, and soufflé for dessert paired with an extensive French wine list.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the largest Disney park — consider renting an ECV (electric convenience vehicle) for elderly family members. The International Food & Wine Festival (if running in June) adds even more tasting kiosks around World Showcase. Book Remy's Ratatouille Adventure Lightning Lane early as it sells out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios — Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure — Arrive at rope drop with Early Entry to head directly to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. First priority: Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run (choose your role as pilot, gunner, or engineer). Then join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance — arguably Disney's most immersive attraction ever built, featuring life-size AT-AT walkers and a full-scale Star Destroyer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Build Your Own Lightsaber at Savi's Workshop — Book the premium Savi's Workshop experience in advance (approximately $250 per person) to hand-build a custom lightsaber with your choice of hilt style, kyber crystal, and sleeve. A deeply immersive 20-minute guided ceremony. Afterward, visit Docking Bay 7 for a snack and explore Black Spire Outpost shops for exclusive Star Wars merchandise.
day_by_day.evening: Hollywood Studios Evening Entertainment — Catch the nighttime spectacular Disney Movie Magic projection show on the Chinese Theatre. Experience Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster with Lightning Lane during lower-crowd evening hours. End the night with Fantasmic! — a spectacular outdoor water, fire, and projection show at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (reserve a Fantasmic! dining package for guaranteed premium seating).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at The Hollywood Brown Derby Lounge — Enjoy Continental breakfast with freshly baked pastries, smoked salmon, and signature cocktails in the iconic Hollywood-themed setting.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Oga's Cantina in Galaxy's Edge — The only bar inside a Disney park, serving exotic Star Wars-themed cocktails (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), limited bites, and featuring DJ R-3X spinning intergalactic beats. Reserve well in advance — slots fill within minutes of release.
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Hollywood Brown Derby — Hollywood Studios' flagship fine dining restaurant. Enjoy the legendary Cobb Salad (invented here), pan-seared sea bass, and premium cuts of beef in an elegant Old Hollywood atmosphere with original celebrity caricatures lining the walls.

day_by_day.notes: Savi's Workshop reservations open 60 days in advance and sell out extremely fast — book the moment your window opens or contact Disney's VIP Tour Services to assist. Consider hiring a private Disney VIP Tour Guide for this day ($425–$650/hour, minimum 7 hours) to bypass lines entirely and receive personalized park navigation. Droid Depot (build your own droid, ~$120) is another premium add-on if budget allows.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom — Kilimanjaro Safari & Avatar Experience — Arrive at Early Entry to experience Kilimanjaro Safaris immediately at opening when animals are most active in the cooler morning temperatures. Spot lions, elephants, giraffes, rhinos, and hippos on the expansive 110-acre savanna. Afterward, explore the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail for up-close wildlife encounters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pandora — The World of Avatar — Dedicate the afternoon to the breathtaking Pandora land. Experience Avatar Flight of Passage (Lightning Lane essential — the most in-demand ride at Walt Disney World) for an exhilarating banshee-riding simulation over the alien moon. Follow with Na'vi River Journey for a serene boat ride through bioluminescent rainforest. Explore the floating Hallelujah Mountains landscape and browse Windtraders for unique Pandora-themed keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Tree of Life Awakenings & Rivers of Light — As dusk falls, witness the magical Tree of Life Awakenings — spontaneous projection shows that illuminate the 145-foot tree with hundreds of spirit animals. Attend Rivers of Light: We Are One nighttime spectacular at the Discovery River Amphitheater featuring floating lanterns, water screens, and animal imagery. End with a walk through Discovery Island in the glowing evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tusker House Restaurant — Donald's Safari Breakfast character dining experience featuring African-inspired cuisine including bobotie, pap, and fresh tropical fruits. Meet Donald Duck, Daisy, Goofy, and Mickey in safari attire.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tiffins Restaurant — Animal Kingdom's most upscale dining establishment. Named for the tiffin boxes carried by traveling explorers, this AAA Four Diamond restaurant serves globally inspired cuisine including sustainable seafood, exotic game meats, and artisan desserts in a beautifully curated space adorned with original artwork from Disney Imagineers.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nomad Lounge adjacent to Tiffins — Enjoy craft cocktails, small plates, and an extensive wine list in a relaxed explorer-chic atmosphere. Alternatively, return to your resort for a private in-room dining experience arranged through your concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Book Avatar Flight of Passage Lightning Lane the instant the park opens — it is the single most competitive Lightning Lane selection at Walt Disney World. June heat peaks in the afternoon; the lush canopy of Animal Kingdom provides more shade than other parks, but plan for a brief mid-afternoon rest at the resort if traveling with young children. The Oasis area at park entrance features exotic wildlife worth exploring slowly on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Resort Leisure & Spa Morning — Enjoy a relaxed morning at your boutique resort. Take advantage of the premium pool facilities, order an indulgent in-room breakfast from room service, and schedule spa treatments (massages, facials, or body wraps) at the resort spa or a nearby luxury spa facility. This is a well-deserved rest day after five intensive theme park days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Favorite Park or Second Visit — Use the afternoon to revisit your favorite park for any missed attractions or experiences. Alternatively, explore Disney's BoardWalk — a charming waterfront entertainment district adjacent to EPCOT featuring artisan shops, street performers, dueling pianos at Jellyrolls, and scenic lakeside views. Rent Surrey bikes or take a gondola ride on Disney Skyliner.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Disney VIP Experience or Private Event — Arrange through your concierge a private after-hours experience such as a Behind the Seeds tour at EPCOT's greenhouses, a Keys to the Kingdom backstage tour of Magic Kingdom, or a private fireworks cruise on Seven Seas Lagoon for an unparalleled view of Magic Kingdom's Happily Ever After from the water with a private captain, catered food, and beverages.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious in-room breakfast via room service — freshly squeezed juices, artisan pastries, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and premium coffee or tea delivered to your suite.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Flying Fish on Disney's BoardWalk — An award-winning, AAA Four Diamond restaurant celebrating Florida coastal cuisine. Signature dishes include potato-wrapped red snapper, Wagyu beef, and Florida stone crab claws (seasonal). Elegant atmosphere with an open kitchen.
meals.dinner: Farewell Pre-Finale Dinner at Victoria & Albert's at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa — One of only a handful of AAA Five Diamond restaurants in all of Florida and consistently ranked among the finest restaurants in the United States. A multi-course chef's tasting menu (10–13 courses) featuring the finest seasonal ingredients, rare wines, and impeccable service. Jacket required for gentlemen. Reservations are extremely limited and open 60 days in advance — this is the crown jewel of Disney dining.

day_by_day.notes: Victoria & Albert's requires significant advance planning — if reservations are unavailable through standard channels, contact Disney's VIP Concierge Services or a luxury Disney travel agent immediately. The private fireworks cruise on Seven Seas Lagoon must be booked through Disney's recreation department and accommodates up to 10 guests. This day is intentionally paced to restore energy before the final full day.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning — Park of Choice or Resort Experience — Spend your final morning revisiting your favorite park using remaining Lightning Lane passes, or enjoy a leisurely resort morning. Consider the Magic Kingdom for one final walk down Main Street U.S.A. and a last ride on your favorite attraction. Purchase any remaining souvenirs from World of Disney at Disney Springs (the largest Disney store in the world).
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Shopping & Farewell Stroll — Dedicate the early afternoon to Disney Springs for final souvenir shopping, browsing The Art of Disney gallery for collectible artwork and animation cels, and enjoying the festive atmosphere. Visit Marketplace Co-Op for unique artisan Disney merchandise not found elsewhere.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation — Return to your boutique resort for final packing. Utilize Disney's Resort Airline Check-In service (if available) to check your luggage directly from the resort to your airline, allowing you to travel to the airport without managing bags. Arrange a private luxury transfer back to Orlando International Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at 1900 Park Fare at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort — A beloved character breakfast featuring Cinderella, Prince Charming, the Evil Stepmother, and Stepsisters in a whimsical carousel-themed dining room with an abundant buffet of premium breakfast offerings.
meals.lunch: Lunch at The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — An upscale waterfront restaurant specializing in fresh Florida seafood, prime steaks, and chops. Enjoy dining on the open-air dock with views of the lake and vintage amphicar tours. Try the whole Maine lobster or the captain's platter.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your resort or airport lounge — Enjoy a final relaxed dinner at your resort's signature restaurant before your transfer, or if departing in the evening, dine at the MCO airport's premium lounges or restaurants before your flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Disney's Magical Express luggage service details may have changed — verify current resort-to-airport transfer options with your concierge upon arrival. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer, check-in, and security. Consider purchasing Disney PhotoPass Memory Maker (if not already included) to download all professional photos taken throughout the week by Disney photographers at no additional per-photo cost. This is a wonderful way to preserve every magical memory from your luxury Disney World experience.

query: Disney World Orlando family of 4, $6000, 7 days, June 2026
